# /adhoc-sdlc:plan

Read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/adhoc-sdlc/SKILL.md` (Read tool): sections "Plan file", "Language", "Commands", "Execution tasks". For the file contract see `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/adhoc-sdlc/reference.md` (Helper, Files).

Interactive command: it settles the real design decisions with the user, saves the plan file, and finally closes the loop into execution (optional `exec` run that tracks the plan's `## Tasks` through the helper). The file is ONLY a plan; implementation belongs to `exec`, but the plan can launch it right away.

Match the user's language for all output (questions, reports, plan prose). Keep the semantic name and filenames ASCII (the helper normalizes them).

If `AskUserQuestion` fails with an input-validation error, retry the call once with the same content (a transient serialization glitch, not a mistake in your input) before falling back to plain-text questions.

## Argument parsing

From `$ARGUMENTS` extract:
- `--name "..."` short session/task description (the helper normalizes it to a semantic name),
- `--title "..."` human title,
- `--project P` optional project/area token (`[a-z0-9._-]`),
- `--keywords a,b,c` optional keywords (`[a-z0-9-]` tokens).

## Phase 0: mode gate

Before asking, read the project's default modes with the helper: `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/adhoc-sdlc/scripts/adhoc_sdlc.py config --get-modes` (it returns each mode's default; no config file means all OFF). Use those values as the pre-selected answers in the mode-gate question below; the user can still flip any.

After a brief read of the prompt and before planning, ask the user to choose the six modes via `AskUserQuestion`, each with a task-tailored recommendation. Three are orthogonal yes/no toggles; the other three are quality gates. If the surface limits how many questions can be asked at once, pack the three quality gates into a single multi-select so all six modes fit; otherwise ask them however the surface allows:

1. Brainstorming dialog. Yes: run a light inline brainstorm (intent, variants, edge cases, convergence). No: draft the plan yourself, using the Phase 1 anchors as an internal checklist and asking only about critical blockers.
2. Deep code verification. Yes: dispatch a read-only subagent (via the `Agent` tool, `subagent_type: general-purpose`) to check assumptions against the codebase, then analyze its findings and show them to the user. No: handle it yourself and decide whether to read code at all.
3. Test the execution. Yes: pick a method per stack (UI: agent-browser or Playwright depending on availability; logic: the project's unit-test framework), run existing tests and write or adjust unit tests as needed. No: skip tests, but `exec` always runs a final self-check and records the trace in the journal.
4. Quality gates (multi-select, any combination):
   - Plan CoVe. Selected: before saving the plan, verify the draft plan's factual claims and assumptions with CoVe-style independent questions. Not selected: rely on the normal planning review.
   - Strategy Temper. Selected: after Plan CoVe and before saving the plan, run a focused failure-mode pass on the strategy (edge cases, partial failure, retries/idempotency, migration/existing state, integration boundaries, verification gaps, reversibility, security/data safety, architecture responsibility leaks). Not selected: rely on the normal planning review and the required final self-check.
   - Execution CoVe. Selected: before closing execution as done, verify the final report against the diff, journal entries, task completion (`tasks`), and actual verification commands. Not selected: rely on tests plus the required final self-check.

If the user has already said "don't ask" in this session, do not block: the Phase 1 request reading still runs, `plan-cove` and `strategy-temper` are ON, the other four modes take the project defaults read above (`config --get-modes`), and you list the assumed modes explicitly (always a final self-check + journal).

Record the chosen modes (`brainstorming`, `deep-code-verification`, `test-execution`, `plan-cove`, `strategy-temper`, `execution-cove`); they are written into the plan body in Phase 2 as the contract `exec` reads.

## Phase 1: design decisions (intention hardening + judgment)

Before saving the plan, run the `intention-hardening` skill (via the `Skill` tool; skills shipped in this plugin are named `adhoc-sdlc:<name>`) on the request; it always reads the request, also under "don't ask". It returns the goal and success criterion, the load-bearing terms with their source, the interpretations (every narrowing or widening named), the question asked or the assumptions made, and the decision anchors (scope, variants, edge cases, test strategy). Record that result in the existing plan sections: the goal and success criterion in `## Summary`, the interpretations and assumptions in `## Assumptions`, and the user's verbatim request in `## Original Prompt` through the helper's `--prompt` flag (Phase 2).

Use the `SKILL.md` Engineering checklist as a light filter while making these decisions. Apply KISS, YAGNI, DRY with judgment, local conventions first, separation of concerns, cohesion over cleverness, explicit contracts, testability, security/data safety, and evidence-based performance. Put only task-relevant consequences into `## Key Changes` or `## Assumptions`; do not create a checklist report unless the user asks for one.

Think for the user: propose resolutions with a recommendation, verify assumptions in code and data sources instead of guessing, and call out risks and edge cases proactively. For each anchor with an OPEN decision ask the user `AskUserQuestion` (concise, recommendation first, labeled "(rec.)"). Skip an anchor that is obvious or has no variant; do not ask about the obvious. When no anchor has an open decision, say so plainly ("no open design decisions") and move on.

Do not assume decisions silently. If the user explicitly says "don't ask / just do it", do NOT block them with questions, but LIST the adopted resolutions as explicit assumptions (open to veto); never hide them only in the file. Adopted decisions go into the plan sections (Assumptions / Key Changes).

If `plan-cove` is ON, run the `cove` skill (via the `Skill` tool; skills shipped in this plugin are named `adhoc-sdlc:<name>`) on the draft plan before saving the plan body: treat the draft as provisional, verify its factual claims and assumptions against the source of truth for the task, and revise the plan so unverified claims move to `## Assumptions` or are explicitly caveated.

If `strategy-temper` is ON, run the `temper` skill (via the `Skill` tool; skills shipped in this plugin are named `adhoc-sdlc:<name>`) on the draft plan after Plan CoVe and before saving the plan body, using its adhoc-sdlc plan output:
- When risks are worth recording, add `## Tempered Risks` and `## Accepted Risks` sections to the plan body (`condition -> fix` / `condition -> why acceptable`); the fixes must already be incorporated into the plan, not left as a detached TODO.
- A change beyond the plan's goal follows the skill's Goal boundary rule: it does not enter the plan, it waits in `Operator options` for the operator's decision. Taken: state it as `Widening: <change>` and fold it into the plan as a fix. Declined, or under "don't ask": record it under `## Accepted Risks` as `<condition> -> operator option not taken: <change>`.
- Operator options belong in the temper response, outside the plan file.

## Phase 2: save the plan file

1. Create the plan file with the helper:
   ```bash
   python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/adhoc-sdlc/scripts/adhoc_sdlc.py plan \
     --name "<name>" --title "<title>" [--project <P>] [--keywords <a,b>] [--prompt "<verbatim request>"]
   ```
2. CHECK the exit code. On non-zero, read `ERROR/EXPECTED/EXAMPLE` from stderr and fix the call (e.g. unique name, allowed status/keywords/project); do not create the file by hand.
3. Read the returned `plan=...` path and fill the body sections (`## Summary`, `## Key Changes`, `## Tasks`, `## Test Plan`, `## Assumptions`) with `Edit`, incorporating the Phase 1 decisions and any `plan-cove` revisions. Then add a `## Mode` section recording the Phase 0 toggles (`brainstorming`, `deep-code-verification`, `test-execution`, `plan-cove`, `strategy-temper`, `execution-cove`, plus any defaults assumed under "don't ask"). When `strategy-temper` is ON and there are risks worth recording, also add the optional `## Tempered Risks` and `## Accepted Risks` sections; temper's Operator options stay in its response, not in the file. Do NOT touch the frontmatter block.
4. Write `## Tasks` as the execution task list: one task per Key Change plus one verification task (the Test Plan steps and the final self-check), phrased as concrete actions. Each task is an unindented bullet in exactly this form, with unique ids `T1`, `T2`, ... in order:
   ```markdown
   ## Tasks

   - [T1] <first key change as an action>
   - [T2] <second key change as an action>
   - [T3] Verification: <tests and final self-check>
   ```
   Indented sub-bullets and prose inside the section are ignored. A numbered list (`1. ...`) is not read as tasks at all, and any other unindented bullet (for example `- T1 title` or `- [x] title`) or a repeated id makes the helper refuse to create the journal (exit 2). The plan is the definition only: task state lives in the execution journal, so do not tick or edit `## Tasks` during execution.

## Phase 3: close the loop

After saving the plan, ALWAYS close the loop with two points: (1) add/change anything in the plan, (2) run execution. Ask them via `AskUserQuestion` by default (max 2 questions). If the user explicitly asked "don't ask" in this session, ask the same two points concisely as text instead of `AskUserQuestion`; closing the loop is mandatory, only the form adapts.

1. "Add or change anything in the plan?" If yes, apply with `Edit` on the body sections and show the change.
2. "Run execution now?":
   - **YES** -> move into execution (like `/adhoc-sdlc:exec`, see `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/commands/exec.md` for the full task rules):
     1. create the journal with the SAME `--name` as the plan (this is how `exec` continues this very session, not a new one): `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/adhoc-sdlc/scripts/adhoc_sdlc.py execute --name "<name>" --title "<title>"`. The helper loads the plan's `## Tasks` into the journal (`schema: 2`) as `pending` tasks,
     2. read the task list from the helper: `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/adhoc-sdlc/scripts/adhoc_sdlc.py tasks --name "<name>" --format tsv`. If it is empty (a plan without `## Tasks`), add the tasks with `execute --name "<name>" --title "<title>" --task-add "<task title>"` (repeatable) before the first entry; the helper refuses `--append` until the list has a task. The helper's list is the only task list: there is no separate native list to keep. Time pressure or a "skip the list / just do it" request does NOT lift this: no code change before the journal has its tasks,
     3. execute per the plan, task by task (every `execute` call carries `--name` and `--title`): start a task with `execute --name "<name>" --title "<title>" --task T1 --task-status in_progress` (exactly one task `in_progress` at a time), append each significant step with `execute --name "<name>" --title "<title>" --task T1 --append "..." --files <touched files>`, and mark it done right after it is finished with `--task T1 --task-status done` (the helper refuses `done` without an entry or verification for that task). Close the journal only after every task is `done`.
   - **NO** -> show the plan path and suggest `/adhoc-sdlc:exec --name <name>` for later.

## Output

The plan path and a 1-2 sentence summary. If execution was launched, report per the rules (goal, changed, verified, remaining/limitations) plus the journal path.

## Note

This command WRITES to the project corpus `./adhoc-sdlc` through the helper (it creates the plan file, and the journal if execution is launched). It is not read-only: under plan mode, be aware the helper still creates and updates those files via Bash, even though `Edit`/`Write` are gated.
